accepted.title: Square-count-conditioned quantum regularizations converge to the LQG sphere

locator.verified_from: Held MIT PDF footer and actual physical page, verified with pdftotext -layout.

accepted.subject: Probability & Mathematical Physics
accepted.text: Fix c<1, Q=√((25−c)/6), and γ∈(0,2) with Q=2/γ+γ/2. On the Riemann sphere choose a smooth background metric g₀ flat near U=[0,1]², and a Gaussian free field h with its additive constant normalized by ∫hK₀dVol_g₀=0, where K₀ is the curvature of g₀. For each dyadic square S⊂U let h_S be its spatial average and Z_h(S)=exp(h_S/Q)·side(S). Let P¹ be the terminal dyadic squares satisfying Z_h(S)≤1 and Z_h(S′)>1 for every strict dyadic ancestor S′⊃S. Put h_P=E[h | (h_S)_{S∈P¹}], interpreted for each realized finite partition as the Gaussian projection onto these averages. Conditional on #P¹=n, define g_n=exp(2(h_P/Q+C_n))g₀ with C_n=(1/4)log n−(3/4)log Vol_{exp(2h_P/Q)g₀}(sphere). As n→∞ through values with positive conditioning probability, does the law of this quantum surface converge to a γ-LQG sphere of some deterministic positive total volume, in the quantum-surface topology specified in the source (vague convergence of volume measures after its conformal cylinder normalization)?
accepted.scope_review: Exact ε=1 and n→∞ order retained. This is convergence of quantum surfaces/area measures, not a claim of convergence of the Riemannian distance to the canonical LQG metric. Definitions2.6.1–2.6.5 and the explicit cylinder interpretation pp73–75 read in full. Feasible square counts are required, rather than conditioning on zero-probability integers. The reference in Question2.7.4 and split discussion record2b351… are merged, not numbered twice.
accepted.literature_finding: The counterpart Brownian loops and central charge paper explicitly labels the same assertion Claim6.10 and says it is not formally proved. The 2024 non-smooth Polyakov–Alvarez paper gives uniform loop-mass asymptotics under bounded/precompact conformal-factor hypotheses, which does not establish this square-count-conditioned n→∞ sphere limit. Current author publication list includes those works and 2025/2026 Yang–Mills work, without a claimed closure of this exact limit. Targeted current primary retrieval found no exact closure; this is a bounded status assessment.
accepted.status_grade: B: exact source conjecture and counterpart explicitly heuristic; current primary progress audited without an exact closure
accepted.duplicate_review: Full4825-catalog retrieval found Q196 on transience of a whole-plane supercritical square-adjacency graph, Q37 on LQG geodesic removability, and Q2895–2897 on spectral questions; none is the finite square-count-conditioned subcritical sphere limit. No cross-batch equivalent found.
